admission.justification: General cross-harness confirmation versus per-seat Antigravity data-folder isolation was explicitly weighed under D1014, and the chosen design constrains all future role-launch confirmation, brief-preamble, and turn-end mismatch handling across harnesses.

alternatives.option: Enforce a general, harness-agnostic launch-time server-binding check (create without prompt, confirm exclusive live binding under the harness, retry once, then refuse leaving zero live seats) paired with an opening-brief server_info self-check and zero-wake IDENTITY MISMATCH: pass-through to the parent.
alternatives.reason: Developer ruling D1014 chose a general defense across every harness rather than a single-harness workaround, turning standing order D1011 into product code.

alternatives.option: Isolate Antigravity seats with a harness-specific per-seat data folder or Antigravity-only launch workaround.
alternatives.reason: Developer ruling D1014 rejected a harness-specific fix because seat identity verification protects against cross-seat misbinding on any harness without maintaining per-harness storage workarounds.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A harness repeatedly fails general binding confirmation at an unacceptable refusal rate even after upstream revival fixes, and the developer explicitly authorizes harness-specific session isolation.

consequences: Every eager-harness start pays a bounded server-binding confirmation poll (up to 5.0 s, skipping the legacy 6 s blind sleep on confirmation) and keeps a single automatic retry under the same requestId.

Every role seat's opening brief carries the mandatory server_info self-check and IDENTITY MISMATCH: termination rule, and the turn-end plug-in delivers mismatch lines straight to the parent without wake messages.
Hosts without /proc fall back to (agentId, requestId) confirmation without ancestry inspection and disclose ancestrySkippedReason=proc-unavailable in the launch receipt.
context: In incident 261112-BUG-L50 (issue row 731), Antigravity 1.5.17 revived another live conversation inside a newly started seat's process, causing the new seat to receive a foreign agents-remember-task server, tools, and identity even though Agents Remember's launch inputs were correct.
decider: Developer D1014 (option 2), translated into BUG-R51@v1 and plan ruling by Architect 97e0320d (2026-11-25).
